incoming.title: Experiential
incoming.text: Provided personal experience with axillary odor surgery. Stated that surgery often causes noticeable scars.

incoming.title: Applicational
incoming.text: Identified those who experience recurrence after surgery as target customers.

outgoing.title: Treatment
outgoing.text: Provides a solution to potential remaining odor after surgery without causing further harm to skin. Provides non-scarring odor control option.

outgoing.title: Psychosocial
outgoing.text: Addressed the social pressure caused by underarm odor via educational initiatives. This is more relevant for those experiencing recurrence after surgery as they likely have more severe cases.

nodes.name: Dermatologist
nodes.detail: Dr. Xia, Dr. Zhou, Dr. Hu

incoming.title: Experiential
incoming.text: Provided insights of patients' experiences of conventional solutions. Stated how many people saw underarm odor as a disease. Shared clinical observations of the effects of underarm odor on mental wellbeing. Emphasized understanding the mechanism behind underarm odor.

incoming.title: Technical
incoming.text: Pointed us in the direction of TCM and surgery as alternative solutions. Provided medical expertise and critical research paper that guided our research. Explained how dermatologists notice signs of early emotional distress.

incoming.title: Ethical
incoming.text: Highlighted the importance of reassuring patients that underarm odor is not a disease. Inspired our Xiang'an community seminar.

outgoing.title: Treatment
outgoing.text: Offers a safer treatment option compared to conventional products. Offers a product that prevents portrayal of underarm odor as something that is abnormal.

outgoing.title: Technical
outgoing.text: Inspires new dermatological solutions for underarm odor by using mechanism-based solution. Supports dermatologists in better evaluating if patients require further psychiatric support.

outgoing.title: Psychosocial
outgoing.text: Promoted understanding that underarm odor is not a disease or something to be ashamed of.

incoming.title: Technical
incoming.text: Provided insights on protein stability in the underarm environment. Evaluated our proposed strategies. Inspired us to conduct safety testing.

incoming.title: Applicational
incoming.text: Eliminated spray product format. Prompted us to carry out research for safety of de novo proteins.

outgoing.title: Technical
outgoing.text: Provides case study for protein activity and safety in skincare products.

incoming.title: Technical
incoming.text: Introduced us on the binder design workflow. Directed us in direction of precursor binder. Validated the feasibility of our idea.

outgoing.title: Technical

incoming.title: Technical
incoming.text: Suggested periplasmic expression using the DsbA signal peptide.

outgoing.title: Technical
outgoing.text: Validates his proposed solution.

incoming.title: Technical
incoming.text: Told us that de novo proteins were not more likely to cause an allergic reaction. Suggested us to carry out in silico safety screening of our protein. Suggested us to carry out wet lab testing of proteins' immunogenicity.

incoming.title: Applicational
incoming.text: Inspired us to create a simplified workflow platform for in silico safety screening.

outgoing.title: Technical
outgoing.text: Online safety screening workflow platform could support future iGEM teams and possibly immunologists to evaluate immunogenicity risks.
